result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of formal crossing infrastructure at a signalized intersection, with no marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals visible. While sidewalks are present, they show signs of wear and pavement degradation, and parked vehicles along the curb may obstruct sightlines for those attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to indicate where pedestrians should cross at this signalized intersection, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection foreground

hazards.name: Poor pavement condition
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven road and sidewalk surfaces create trip hazards and may cause vehicles to swerve unexpectedly.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway and sidewalk in the foreground

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra or ladder style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers by moving the waiting area past the line of parked cars.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross.

result.summary: The image shows an urban residential street with integrated trolley tracks and sidewalks on both sides. While there is a traffic signal, the lack of marked crosswalks and the presence of tracks in the roadway create significant hazards for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Embedded Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: The metal tracks in the roadway create an uneven surface that is a trip hazard for pedestrians and a slip/trap hazard for cyclists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway extending into the distance.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at this signalized intersection, which fails to provide a designated and visible path for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground intersection area.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Refuge
hazards.description: The wide roadway lacks a median or refuge island, increasing the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic during a crossing.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with sidewalks and faded crosswalk markings at an intersection. The environment lacks modern safety infrastructure such as high-visibility markings, ADA-compliant curb ramps, and dedicated pedestrian signals.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The existing transverse crosswalk lines are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway crossing

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb near the intersection may block the view of pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to increase visibility for drivers.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection to improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at the crossing points to ensure accessibility.
